question: Which of the following rivers was once known as the “Sorrow of Bengal”?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Damodar.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Damodar is an east-flowing river with a rift valley **due to down warping.
 
• Down warp denotes a segment of the earth’s crust that is broadly bent downward.
 
• It occupies the eastern margins of the Chotanagpur Plateau where it flows through a rift valley and finally joins the Hugli.
 
• The Barakar is its main tributary.
 
• **Once known as the ‘sorrow of Bengal’.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Damodar has been now tamed by the **Damodar Valley Corporation, a multipurpose project.**
 
• **The Bokaro and Konar are two of the many tributaries of the northeastern Indian river, Damodar.**
 
• **It rises in the Chota Nagpur plateau in the heart of the state of Bihar.**
 
• It travels 368 miles (592 km) through West Bengal on a mainly easterly trajectory before merging with the Hugli (Hooghly) River in the southwest of Kolkata (Calcutta).
 
• The most significant coal and mica mining regions in India are located in the Damodar valley, which is located near the boundary between Bihar and West Bengal.
 
• This region has long seen vigorous industrial growth.
 
• **Most of the largest coalfields (Jharia, Raniganj, and Giridih) are open-pit mines, making them simple to exploit.**
